title: Implement groupwise() and layer_axial_lines()
description:
Hello. This implements:
- `groupwise()` to set the Vega "group" reference. I named it `groupwise()` because I found `prop_group()` to be confusing. An alternative could be `from_group()`.
- `layer_axial_lines()` to draw vertical or horizontal lines.

I added support for the rule mark in order to draw the lines.  In the future, we'll be able to use the rule mark to implement something like `layer_sloped_lines()`, but this needs to be fixed first: https://github.com/trifacta/vega/issues/123. Also, it was necessary to prevent ggvis from writing a "from" tag to a mark in the case where no property makes use of data.

Here is an example of using a group property:

``` r
ggvis(faithful) %>%
  layer_histograms(~eruptions) %>%
  emit_rects(props(
    x := 0, x2 := groupwise("width", mult = 0.5),
    y := 0, y2 := groupwise("height", mult = 0.5),
    fill := "red"
  ))
```

![groupwise](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4465050/7329984/ee5517a6-eae6-11e4-8ab1-823281b67f68.png)

As for `layer_axial_lines()`, it will draw one horizontal line for each `y` data point, and one vertical line for each `x` data point. Here the vertical lines are drawn from a data set while the horizontal line is set with `:=`.

``` r
lines_data <- data.frame(values = c(2, 4.5))
ggvis(faithful) %>%
  layer_histograms(~eruptions) %>%
  layer_axial_lines(data = lines_data,
    x = ~values, y := 80,
    stroke := "red", strokeWidth := 4
  )
```

![axial](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4465050/7329989/fa57e952-eae6-11e4-9a26-c766de64f108.png)

Let me know if you're interested in this PR and I'll send the copyright form.

title: Add inter-group coordination to transform_bin
description:
This adds inter-group coordination to `transform_bin`, so that when there are multiple groups, they'll have the same binning boundaries. It's probably easier to look at the changed transform_bin.R file, rather than the diff.

This dispatches on the transform (via `apply_transform`) and then the data object type (via `compute_transform_bin`).

The inter-group determination of binwidth is done in `apply_transform.transform_bin`. @hadley, do you think we should have a pattern of functions that makes it more clear when it does inter-group operations vs. intra-group operations? I'm thinking of ggplot2, where each stat has `calculate_groups()` and `calculate()`. The way it's done here doesn't have that clear a delineation.

Other notes:
- The inter-group coordination could be added as an option to the transform (this may be useful for faceted plots).
- It would be nice to have a data-type-agnostic way of checking a variable's type. For example, in `apply_transform.transform_bin`, I want to do `is.numeric(data[[xvar]])`, but that only works for data frames; it fails for `split_data_dflist` objects.

title: prop: reactives are always treated as variables
description:
This branch makes it so a prop is constant if and only if it's a constant (atomic value). Reactives are now always treated as variable props.
- Previously, a calculated column could have a different length than the data, and this would result in `Error in .subset2(.subset2(x, colname), i) : subscript out of bounds`. Now if a calculated column is automatically replicated to the length of the data; if it has a length that doesn't integer-multiply to the length of the data, it throws an error (see the new tests).
- The last two examples in interactive.r have changed; you can't have a reactive prop with `constant=FALSE` anymore. Previously, the strings returned by the input would pick out columns in the data. Now, a map function, `as.name`, converts the string to a symbol, which, when eval'ed with the data frame, picks out the column. We may want to consider adding something to make this a little easier to understand.
- For cases where a reactive prop uses `scale=TRUE`, the legend doesn't seem to be updated when the data changes. For example, see the third-from-last example in interactive.R, "Constant values, on a scale". The legend doesn't change when the data changes -- but it did prior to this commit.

Some cleanup of examples and documentation is still needed.

title: Add interface for hover, update, enter, exit properties
description:
This branch makes it possible to do things like this:

```
ggvis(mtcars, 
  props(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, size.hover := 400, size.update := 100, fill.hover := "red"),
  mark_symbol()
)
```

Notice that in the case above, `size.update` is needed but `fill.update` isn't. This is because `fill.update` has been set via the default props for mark_symbol, and is therefore in the vega spec, but `size.update` hasn't been added this way (it's unspecified in the spec).

Before this is merged, some tests will have to be fixed, and some docs should be updated.

title: ggvis.renderer option to control default renderer
specify height in call to internal viewer
description:
Formerly the RStudio Viewer pane maximized to take all available vertical space. This was problematic especially for the case of users configured with the Console in the top-right pane. As of RStudio v0.98.423 the viewer function takes an additional height parameter that can be used to request a desired height (excluding the parameter simply uses the current pane height). RStudio will attempt to provide the requested height subject to the constraint of the opposing pane staying at least 160 pixels high (7 lines of text in the Console).

This change hard-codes the requested height to 600 pixels (about what's currently necessary to show a ggvis plot without extra interaction controls). There are two additional refinements we'll ultimately want to make:
- Request less space once we've hidden the standard renderer/download controls. I did some testing and discovered that on an 800 pixel high monitor the ideal height is about 400 pixels so this is probably a good number to shoot for.
- Request some additional space for interaction controls when they are present. We'll also want to do some work to minimize how much vertical space is occupied by interaction controls (e.g. by trying to get two controls per line).

Note that if a height request can't be satisfied there are two possible remedies: (1) ggvis could detect the window height and scale the plot down accordingly; or (2) The window could be allowed to scroll which would serve as a prompt for the user to manually resize the pane as they see fit.

One other change here is the querying of the ggvis.view_internal option to allow the user to specify that they always want plots viewed in an external browser. Wasn't exactly sure how to integrate this with the new opts() function but it seems like this would be desirable.

# .brush prop adds prop that's used when an object is brushed.

  mark_symbol(props(size.brush := 200)),

Right now, brushing only triggers `.brush` props, but we'll obviously want to add the ability to send information back to the server.

title: Fix grouped df in dynamic view
description:
In light of #71, we should push grouped data spec in initial spec so updates on source data could flow in consequent updates. This would also address #154 and #150.

The changes are that we always attempt to push an initial version of data and defs during spec creation. In consequent updates with `ggvis_data` message, we only updates the "source" data from `message.value[0]`. Note for grouped data, `message.name!=message.value[0].name`.

I think the following example verifies that this fix works as data can be updated dynamically:
https://gist.github.com/saurfang/11d2cc1c6c041bcfa721

```
runGist("11d2cc1c6c041bcfa721")
```

title: Scale datetime domain approriately
description:
When domains are of type datetime, the `unlist` operation automatically coerce the values into timestamps in seconds. Using `format_vec_d3json` to proactively cast datatype before range calculation.

Quick example to reproduce the problem:

```
library(lubridate)
view_dynamic(data.frame(date=ymd(20140101)+months(1:5), value=runif(5)) %>% 
ggvis(~date, ~value) %>% 
layer_points() %>% 
set_dscale("x", "datetime", nice="month"))
```

Let me know if you have any suggestions or concerns. Also I can probably get CLA back to you guys by Friday.

title: Fix grouped_df in dynamic view
description:
Redo the PR #155 because master got updated and I botched the upstream merge. Again this is to allow ggvis to work with `grouped_df` in dynamic view.

The root cause was that data for `grouped_df` are broken down to source data and a `flatten` data transform verb. The latter part must be included as part of the initial plot spec. So the naive fix could just be that we always materialize dataset when constructing the initial spec.

One of the concerns was that we would send dataset twice during the initialization phase because a `ggvis_data` message will also be sent during setup. So I made a separate logic just for `grouped_df` such that everything else continue just sending its name but `grouped_df` would include the additional `flatten` transform.

Not sure if this is the right trade between code complexity and performance.

Lastly, for this to work, we need to make sure when processing `ggvis_data` we use the correct dataset name for `grouped_df` in `shiny-ggvis.js`

Here's a simple example to reproduce:

```
view_dynamic(mtcars %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg) %>%
             group_by(cyl) %>%
             layer_paths())
```
